_readme: THE COMMUNITY REGISTRY. One file, one pull request — that is the whole
contribution path. Add an object to `entries` and open a PR against
website/docs/data/community.json; nothing else needs touching and no
Fields: kind (build|scene|skill|part|tool), title, who, url, blurb, tags,
(a path under website/assets/ or an absolute URL) and date (YYYY-MM).
Everything below is from the reference build and is MARKED AS SUCH. There
are no outside entries yet — the page says so rather than inventing any.

entries.title: MABEL v1.0 — the reference build
entries.blurb: 56 DoF, 59 motors, $8,722 of parts, assembled in a weekend. Every number in this manual was measured on this robot.

entries.title: 3-module swerve base
entries.blurb: Delta-layout holonomic base on REV MAXSwerve. Translates in any direction without turning first — the reason the arrow keys strafe.

entries.title: ORCA hand, 17 DoF
entries.blurb: Open-source tendon hand, 16 Feetech servos and a wrist on one TTL chain. Printed, not machined.

entries.title: 40 simulation scenes
entries.blurb: Homes, cafés, warehouses and four New York streets with scripted traffic. Each one is an MJCF you can drop a policy into.

entries.title: ACT, DiT, π₀ and π₀.₅
entries.blurb: Four policy architectures behind one trainer. ACT and the diffusion policy train on the robot's own Jetson.

entries.title: Data Curation studio
entries.blurb: Score a dataset, blade the bad takes on a timeline, export LeRobot v2.1. Runs in a browser.

challenges.title: Build the base, post the video
challenges.goal: Three swerve modules, one chassis, driving under its own power.
challenges.why: It is the first subassembly that MOVES, and the first place the manual is likely to be wrong. Every build that gets here makes chapter 02 better.

challenges.title: A scene we have not thought of
challenges.goal: One MJCF the robot can be dropped into — your kitchen, your lab, your loading bay.
challenges.why: Forty scenes is not a lot of world. A scene is a single XML file and a PR.

challenges.title: Teach it something with your own hands
challenges.goal: Fifty clean demonstrations of one task, curated and exported.
challenges.why: The bottleneck is not the model, it is the data. Fifty good episodes of anything is a real contribution.
